note: Goose is not installed on the machine this was extracted on, so the rule comes from the release's own source archive rather than from a running binary -- which spec section 5 allows ('the application's own shipped code') and spec question 6 requires, since the alternative was demoting the row. Nothing here was measured on the wire.
document_is_bare_config_evidence: load_custom_providers (declarative.rs:330) reads every *.json in custom_providers/ and calls deserialize_provider_config, which is serde_json::from_value straight into DeclarativeProviderConfig. Goose's own writer, create_custom_provider (declarative_providers.rs:170-241), builds that struct and writes serde_json::to_string_pretty of it. There is no wrapper key -- so the {"custom_provider": {...}} envelope MCC's serialiser produced until 6.84.0 was a struct with every required field missing.
file_name_evidence: custom_provider_file_path (declarative_providers.rs:117) joins custom_providers_dir() with format!("{}.json", id); validate_provider_id allows a leading lowercase ASCII letter, digit or '_' and then lowercase ASCII, digits, '_' and '-'.
required_keys_evidence: DeclarativeProviderConfig (declarative.rs:148-193): the five listed have neither #[serde(default)] nor an Option type. Everything else carries a default or is Option with #[serde(default)].
engine_evidence: enum ProviderEngine with #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")] plus #[serde(alias = "openai_compatible")] / "ollama_compatible" / "anthropic_compatible", and FromStr accepting the same six spellings (declarative.rs:95-113).

base_url_and_path.evidence: openai::from_declarative_config (openai.rs:931-941) parses base_url, takes the host from it, and uses config.base_path when set, else derive_base_path(url.path()), whose empty-path answer is 'v1/chat/completions'. So MCC writes the proxy root in base_url and names the path explicitly -- which is what BaseUrlShape.SPLIT_HOST_PATH is.

credential.resolved_from: Goose's own secret store, not the process environment
credential.evidence: ConfigKeyResolver::resolve_key (goose/src/providers/custom_provider_config.rs) is self.config.get_secret(key) -- the keyring, or secrets.yaml under GOOSE_DISABLE_KEYRING. from_declarative_config bails with 'missing required key {}' when requires_auth is true and the key cannot be resolved. A literal written anywhere in this document is ignored.

model_required_keys_evidence: struct ModelInfo (goose-provider-types/src/base.rs:246-270). The six listed are Option<T> *without* #[serde(default)], so serde requires the key to be present even when the value is null; 'reasoning' and the three skip_serializing_if members carry defaults. There is no 'id', no 'output_limit', no 'supports_vision' and no 'supports_tools' -- the four keys MCC wrote until 6.84.0.
model_cost_unit_evidence: 'Cost per token for input in USD (optional)' / 'Cost per token for output in USD (optional)'. MCC's ladder carries prices per million, so every price is divided by 1000000 before it is written.
